say: You're going to work at the bottom of the North Sea. The trip down takes minutes. The trip back up takes days.
Saturation divers live in a sealed chamber on a ship, kept at the same pressure as the depth they work at, for up to twenty-eight days.
Problem one: talking. You breathe helium mixed with oxygen, and it makes every voice sound like a cartoon.
Problem two: food. Your meals come in through a tiny airlock, like the pass-through window at a bank.
Problem three: leaving. Your body is soaked with dissolved gas. Come up too fast and it bubbles out of your blood. So decompression takes several days.
And if the ship catches fire, you can't just jump overboard. There's a lifeboat for that, and it's pressurized too.
